title: Bipartisan support for NOAA's Digital Coast Program to Protect Coastal Areas from Climate Change - NewsBreak
text: Washington, D.C. — Lawmakers from opposite coasts are teaming up to support America’s coastal regions, and Orange County could see major benefits. Representative Dave Min of California, along with Representative Rob Wittman of Virginia and Senators Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, introduced new bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s Digital Coast Program. The bill aims to help coastal communities across the country adapt to climate change with better tools and data. According to Rep. Min, the Digital Coast Program delivers more than just science—it fuels job creation and resilience in areas like Orange County. “NOAA’s Digital Coast Program provides essential research and data to address the adverse effects of the climate crisis, all while creating thousands of high tech jobs around America,” Min said. “I’m proud to be leading the charge to protect Orange County’s beautiful coastline.” In Virginia, where coastline communities face extreme weather and aging infrastructure, Rep. Wittman emphasized the practical benefits. “Virginia’s First District is home to vibrant coastal communities that rely on cutting-edge data and resources to thrive,” Wittman said. “This vital program collects and distributes data that will help mitigate future weather-related issues and provide communities with the tools they need to expand and plan for the future.” Senator Baldwin highlighted the importance of the program for the Great Lakes region. “The Great Lakes are essential to the Wisconsin way of life and our economy,” Baldwin said. “Our local communities need tools and information to address them, keep families safe, and support our local businesses.” Senator Murkowski echoed the call for readiness in the face of climate change, noting that the Digital Coast Program “has proven to be a vital resource” for decision-makers in coastal areas like Alaska. National organizations are voicing strong support. Sue Schwartz of the American Planning Association praised the program as “innovative, collaborative, efficient, bipartisan, and cost-effective,” while Chad Berginnis of the Association of State Floodplain Managers said it “ensures continued access to the data, tools, and training that coastal managers rely on every day.”
